title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs', a draft toward tame topology. There is a set M of elementary pieces, which behave like cells or strata. M carries three relations:
- a partial order ≤ (subobject or incidence);
- a second order ≪ ('lies in the shadow of'), with Omb(X) = {Y | Y ≪ X}, a closure-like down-set;
- a compatibility relation ≭.
Figures of finite type F ∈ 𝓕 are determined by their sets of pieces F̃ ⊂ M. On the previous page (AE4) the relation ≪ on figures is defined from ≪ on M: G ≪ F iff every X ∈ G̃ satisfies X ≪ Y for some Y ∈ F̃. Axiom C6 (AE6) says that for compatible X, Y, X ≪ Y implies X ≤ Y. This is a 'frontier condition': being in the closure of a compatible piece means being a face of it.

This page draws the consequences.
- Corollary 1: the pieces of one figure are pairwise compatible, so on F̃ the orders ≤ and ≪ coincide.
- Corollary 2: for compatible figures F, G, F ≪ G ⇔ F ≤ G. The direction ⇐ is general. For ⇒, by AE4/C4 one reduces to pieces X ∈ F̃ and Y ∈ G̃ with X ≪ Y, and applies C6.
- Consequence: for each F, the 'multi-shadow' Multomb(F) = {Omb(Y) | Y ∈ F̃} is in bijection with F̃, compatibly with the orders.
- To see that Multomb(F) is itself a figure in P(M), its 'open strata' must be nonempty: Ỹ⁰ = Ỹ \ ⋃_{Y' ∈ F̃, Y' < Y} Ỹ'. This holds because Y ∈ Ỹ⁰. If Y were in Ỹ' with Y' < Y, then Y ≪ Y' ≪ Y, and antisymmetry (with C6 / Corollary 1) forces Y = Y'.
- Finally, (129) is the map M → P(M), X ↦ Omb(X) = M_{≪X}, the principal down-set map of the poset (M, ≪). It is injective because ≪ is antisymmetric; the inclusion order on P(M) induces ≪, which a priori would only be a preorder. The figures Multomb(F) are exactly the images of the F̃.

Aim: show that figures can be reconstructed from (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) and realized concretely as stratified 'sets of closures' inside P(M). The next page proves that F ≤ G ⇔ Multomb(F) ⊂ Multomb(G), and that Multomb commutes with ∨ and ∧ for compatible figures.
errors: Corollary 2 implicitly needs that X ≤ Y with Y ∈ G̃ forces X ∈ G̃, so that F ≤ G follows from piecewise ≤. That is, G̃ must be ≤-downward closed (equivalently F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃, which is only made explicit on the next page). This is not stated here.
Minor: the definition of Ỹ⁰ on this page uses Ỹ both for Omb(Y) and, elsewhere, for the set of pieces of a figure. The notation is overloaded but harmless.

ideas.what: Axiom C6: for compatible pieces, being in the shadow (closure) of Y implies being ≤ Y. Hence ≤ and ≪ coincide on the pieces of a figure.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications (closure of a stratum is a union of strata; specialization order equals face order)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology and stratified structures informally, but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Embedding X ↦ Omb(X) = M_{≪X} of the poset into its power set. Figures become sets of principal down-sets, with nonempty open strata Ỹ⁰.
ideas.modern_name: Principal down-set (Yoneda-type) embedding of a poset; Alexandrov topology / face poset of a cell complex

ideas.what: Reconstruction of figures of finite type (𝓕, ≤, ≪) from the structure (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) on elementary pieces, via Multomb.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial axiomatics of tame/stratified spaces (cf. o-minimal cell decompositions, exit-path posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished axiomatic, purely order-theoretic foundation for tame topology. 'Figures' are reconstructed from a poset of pieces with two orders and a compatibility relation. This page contains only routine order-theoretic lemmas, but the overall axiomatic programme (axioms C1–C6, AE4–AE6, Multomb) does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: la projection de Multomb(F) sur F̃ est bijective, et respecte les relations d'ordre (naturelles ≤)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Might be compared with combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, posets of strata in o-minimal geometry). However, nothing on this page goes beyond standard poset facts.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is routine order theory: the frontier condition implies the two orders coincide, and the down-set embedding is injective. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft.
transcription_corrections: The margin NB is written diagonally and is largely illegible. It appears to say that showing Y ∈ Ỹ⁰ uses C6: for Y, Y' ∈ F̃ with Y' ≠ Y and Y' ≤ Y (equivalently Y' ≪ Y), one cannot have Y ≪ Y'.
The equation label '(129)' is overwritten in the image. The next page cites it as '(4.3.9)', so the label is uncertain.
The parenthetical under Ỹ⁰ reads '(ou encore, Y'≪Y, Y'≠Y)', glossing the strict inequality Y' ⪇ Y.
